threads.body: The aggregated batch query text concatenates the sanitized text of every request with no upper bound on length. The analogous redisson Redis-batch implementation caps the joined query text at 32 KB (`LIMIT = 32 * 1024`, see `RedissonRequest.java:44,160`) specifically to avoid emitting an enormous `db.query.text`/`db.statement` attribute for large pipelines. Since this PR is a slice of the same Redis batch work, consider applying a similar length cap here so a very large batch does not produce an unbounded span attribute.

threads.body: The "empty" batch scenario asserts `db.operation.batch.size = 0`, but this attribute is never emitted for an empty batch. `createBatch` computes `batchSize = 0` for an empty list (`requests.size() != 1`), and `DbClientAttributesExtractor.onStartCommon` only sets `DB_OPERATION_BATCH_SIZE` when `batchSize != null && batchSize > 1`. So under stable semconv the attribute is absent, and `equalTo(DB_OPERATION_BATCH_SIZE, 0)` evaluates to `assertThat((Long) null).isEqualTo(0L)`, which fails. The plain `:javaagent:test` run passes because the old-semconv branch has no batch-size assertion, but the `testStableSemconv` task (wired into `check`) exercises this and will fail. Drop `.batchSize(0)` so the empty scenario expects no batch-size attribute (matching the single-command scenario).
